To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a network model of hippocampal function can simulate the effects of scopolaming on free recall and recognition in humans, and that the model predicts that scopolaming should enhance proactive interference during paired associate learning.
a network model of hippocampal function can simulate the effects of scopolmine on human memory.

(1) scopolamine impairs encoding of novel input patterns but not retrieval of previously stored patterns, (2) the impairment is selective to free recall but not item recognition, (3) the model predicts a list-strength effect in free recall but not in recognition, and (4) the model predicts that the effects of scopolmine on memory are asymmetric, with greater impairment of retrieval than encoding.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of acetylcholinergic modulation in the hippocampus and its role in the formation and retrieval of memory.
the effects of scopolame on the encoding and retrieval of information by the human hippocampus.
the role of acetylcholinergic input to the hippocampal system in the acquisition and consolidation of declarative memory.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
scopolamine impairs the encoding but not the retrieval of new items, and that this impairment is specific to free recall but not to recognition.
the network model provides a framework to explain how the effects of scopolmine can be used to probe the role of the hippocampus in human episodic memory.
the model is a good model of the human brain and the effects of scopolmine on the brain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
scopolamine impairs free recall of items encoded under its influence by selectively weakening the attractor states for those items.
the hippocampus is a system of memory storage and retrieval, and scopolamine is a drug that interferes with the storage of memory.
scopolamine blocks the formation of attractor states in the model and this blockade is more severe in the CA3 than in the CA1 subregions of the hippocampus.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the network model of hippocampus is a useful tool for understanding the neural mechanisms of memory and for predicting the effects of neuromodulators on memory.
a simple network model can replicate many of the effects of scopolamide on free recall and recognition in humans.
a network model of hippocampal memory, incorporating the cellular effects of scopolame, can replicate many of the memory impairments observed in human subjects.
